## Data Science and Economics

I am a **Senior Economist/Data Scientist** in the **Health Services Management Team** at **SWICA**, one of Switzerland's largest health insurers. I lead projects on healthcare financing, develop shared-savings and value-based models with provider partners, mostly within **Managed Care** contracts, and measure whether they actually change outcomes.

My role is to **design financing models from claims data** that create value and contain costs. I also **evaluate whether our interventions actually work**, with quasi-experimental designs and causal machine learning. We published our study on vitamin D testing in *BMC Health Services Research*, and it was picked up by Sonntagszeitung and Tages-Anzeiger. I like exchanging ideas at national and international conferences in health economics, statistics, and population research.

Before, I was an **Economics researcher** at **the Swiss Institute for Empirical Economic Research (SEW) at the University of St. Gallen**, where I led projects in education economics and applied econometrics. I published some work on gifted students and their positive effects on their peers.

<hr>

## Teaching

Since 2023, I have been **teaching introductory data science with R**, and since 2026, [**Introduction to Programming**](https://aureliensallin.ch/BEcon_4222_Introduction_Programming/) for undergraduate economists at the **University of St. Gallen**. I focus on making statistical concepts accessible and helping students develop practical skills for their future careers in data science, economics, and related fields.

<hr>

## Other interests

When I’m not analyzing data or teaching, I’m likely outdoors, **running and biking** in the Swiss Alps. I’m also passionate about civic engagement and the R community. Since 2023, I’ve been a co-organizer of the **[Zürich R User Group](https://zurich-r-user-group.github.io/)**. In 2024, I was elected to the **audit commission** of the municipality of Flawil, where I contribute to local democratic oversight.
